claims.text: Pre-sintering ALD can deposit a nanometer-scale Cu or Cu-alloy wetting layer selectively on tungsten surfaces.
An ALD Cu wetting layer will enhance Cu infiltration into a W scaffold.
An ALD Cu wetting layer will enhance interparticle bonding in W–Cu composites.
The intervention will minimize phase separation and void formation in W–Cu composites.
The intervention will preserve the mechanical durability of W–Cu composites under irradiation.
Conventionally sintered or cast W–Cu material containing W particles or connected W regions has interfacial voids and phase separation.
The proposed W–Cu fabrication can be performed below 1000 °C, well below the melting point of W.
The ALD coating promotes atomic interdiffusion at the Cu–W interface.
The ALD coating produces a uniform, conformal Cu–W interface.
The ALD coating reduces interfacial energy barriers and eliminates nucleation sites for voids during sintering.
Enhanced wettability from the ALD layer facilitates uniform Cu infiltration into the W scaffold.
Uniform Cu infiltration reduces phase separation and void formation.
Improved Cu–W interfacial bonding maintains continuous thermal pathways and mechanical integrity under irradiation.
Relative to spark-plasma sintering or vapor-coated W powder processing, ALD-treated W–Cu will have a significantly lower void fraction.
Relative to the named fabrication baselines, ALD-treated W–Cu will have improved interfacial thermal conductance.
Relative to the named fabrication baselines, ALD-treated W–Cu will preserve mechanical durability during simulated irradiation.
Spark-plasma sintering and vapor-coated W powder sintering often leave residual interfacial voids or phase-separated regions.
Residual interfacial voids or phase-separated regions impair thermal transport and durability under irradiation.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome names spark-plasma sintering and vapor-coated W powders as comparators, but the controlled experiment compares ALD-treated material only with an untreated surface under otherwise identical sintering conditions. Thus, the experiment does not directly test the stated comparison against all named baselines.
